theory_questions.question: Container deixis: should a particle run on a body's first line bind the enclosing frame (as the LSP attributes it and catalogers, designers and crews expect) or the next child (as the seed does)? contract.spw places #:claim inside the claim frame and the gate's source check relies on that.
Is there, or should there be, a file-level deixis, so a header stack labels the file (like #![..] or #pragma once) instead of binding to the ^emit card?
Should case, mood and anchor names start with a digit (#!3, #>12a, NGSS K-5), or is letter-first part of what makes a mood a word?
Which names win per aim: lexer deixis, case and mood, or LSP anchor, lens and intent? Should docs pair each grammatical name with a closer term?
Is #! illocutionary force, epistemic status or a general value slot? Is evidentiality a new aim or a closed value set under mood, and how does it relate to claim status?

Which reader name wins for each split sigil (& confluence or subject, ^ integration or ascension, . ground or Subject, = configuration or Set, $ substrate or select), and should physics homonyms keep their names with stated limits?
Is the operator x bound table meant to be total, or are unnamed cells (*[ ], $( ), &( )) intended gaps? Is the ?< > wall a parser bug or a canon error?
Does the prefix-transitive and postfix-reflexive law bind the parser (x!, x? and data~ parse as siblings)? Is standby-then-go the motivating case for ?'s blocking strategy?
Which equivalence does canon mean by === or 'theorem': value, register writes or trace? Should *~X === X become a delay and force law, and & commutativity be stated per spelling?
Should Spw ever assert equality, commutation or isomorphism, or is pairing without identity a deliberate stance?
Should infix a <> b become coupling, and may <> be n-ary? Today only the first two string keys couple, quoted operands keep their quotes, and a <> inside #[ ] is never evaluated.
Are the register frame constructors #[ ], .{ } and @( ) ready to promote? Is #[ ] unordered and unique by law, given the AST keeps order and duplicates?
Should the lexer own a compound list ($%, ##>, =>, <=>, <->, ~<tag>'p') so compounds read one way and parse the same way?

Reach: canon says # owns [ ] and @ owns ( ), while highlighting tags brackets with the prefix operator. Which reach should color show? Do ~> and => carry their sigil's reader role or stay pure connectors?
Should ?, ~, % and ! take a PathRef subject the way ^~'x' does, and should ?( lose its special case? Should doubled heads ??[ !![ **[ be reserved under one closed rule?

Reconcile three readings of the pentad: charge-neutral material (valence-architecture.spw:38-39), edge direction (bias-product.spw:19, where mutate reverts bane) and hazard/error in code (catalog.ts:43-48). Canon's positive/negative and glow similes state no limit. Should sign get its own words?
Should valence words be usable as binding keys (bone:, honk:, swatch names)?
Should the word valence face chemists, clinicians, neuroscientists and linguists, who already own it, or would 'material quality' serve science doors better?
Is the pentad ordered or categorical? Is identical share coverage a twin or the ideal? Can a surface carry two valences?
Canon says runtime quality is four-state with bonk as an overlay while RuntimeValence has five values; has the falsifier fired, and is the CSS and shader projection normative?
What palette expresses material quality, not merit, and does valence get color only in a valence mode? Given the owner's rule, may valence ever mark progress on an arc or a practice ladder?

theory_questions.question: Bias axes are used as relation types ([causes], [needs], [cites], [melts], [feeding]). Should they get a declared set the gate checks, and how should consumers keep mutate --bias from reading them as rewrite patches?
Canon documents a spaced bias form (flow-protocol-sigils.spw:37,66) that yields no edge. Should readBias learn it, or should canon move to the tight form?
Should spw graph read bias edges as typed, directed edges and strip fragments as the LSP does, so cycles are found and valid #anchor targets are not reported broken?
Is an anchor a place in a file or an identity across dated editions? Should uniqueness be scoped per edition, and must rename follow fragment refs (today refactor renames the particle only)?
Should citation typing (CiTO supports and disputes) be edges or source and counter bindings? Can a claim cite a claim, and does a proof count as a source in mathematics?
Should emit continuity be anchored (#> anchors a reader can link to) rather than prose phrases matched anywhere in the packet?
Is % one operator with several profiles (the [0,1] measure, unbounded registry quantities, count families), or does the language need a quantity noun?
Where do ordinal scores live: an ordinal measure family or ?match bands?
Should physical dimensions be checkable, with a dim link on every quantity cell and homogeneity as a falsifier? Is a physical dimension an axis in the dimensional-axes sense?

Will the lexer accept signed, scientific, uncertain or unit-bearing literals ('-' is a ConnectorKind missing from the default map)? Is there a time or timecode literal that cannot be read as a Binding?
Should 'illustrative' become a claim status beside no_invented_numbers, and should basis and strength join #:claim? Meanwhile contraption teaching parameters stay outside claims.
Is ~#lens( ) meant to be tool-visible? The LSP has no APPOSITION branch and the hover reads only '// lens:'. Who owns the patch?
Which new lenses earn a place by recurrence (symmetry and invariance, scale and dimension, equity, applied attention), and should picture readings get their own named apposition?
Do appositions compose? Is an apposition with no host valid? Should named appositions count as volatile aspect in census and LSP volatility?
Should gloss return as a reading separate from apposition (rejected at apposition.spw:52), and should theatre's aside become a bridge row?

Which channel carries readings: # marginalia (hash-resonance.spw:8) or countable appositions? Should tools be fixed so apposition bodies may hold apostrophes and % as canon allows, retiring the cut's ASCII rule?

Is a say line a reading (authored, personal) or a product (derived, cacheable)? May computed say lines be written back? Should a tool compare cold_open with a reader's ~#say, and is the reading set closed across canon or per cut?
Should Spw ship named prior-notation profiles (C, TeX, CSS, R/Stata, MARC, Markdown and chat, classroom) that warn on familiar-but-wrong readings without changing the parse?
Should one stray > or comparison degrade the whole surface, or fail locally with a diagnostic on the offending line?
Will one same-line law govern the medial capsule, empty bindings, inline '# ', caret labels and valence-only capture? Should lexer errors fail success or stay soft as diagnostics?
Is the tight-versus-spaced contrast meant to change the parse (as for bias and ~#k:) or only reading confidence?

Should identifiers accept Unicode letters after NFC normalization, and should curly quotes and guillemets be delimiters or named errors? desugar already rewrites guillemets in the runtime path only (normalize.ts:17-26).
Is the hyphen in identifiers worth the collisions (a->b degrading, x1-x5 varlists, '- item' bullets)?
Should '# ' (drops the rest of the line even mid-line) and #word (a tag) stay as they are, with canon restating the rule as no apostrophe or digit right after #?

For clustering readers: should facet axes and concept hubs become the main way to browse, and how do readers whose tree is the meaning keep their structure? Should indent (one space today) become a declared contract key?
raised_by: owner (physics students and designers cluster conceptually)

theory_questions.question: Should '@handle: text' chat lines be a sanctioned form, or should people and roles get a construct separate from @ so the privacy rule is enforced by syntax? Are pseudonyms salted per session or per channel?
Claim status: a registered mood vocabulary with its own modifier, glyph inlays, spoken names, or never colored? Is the 32-bit modifier budget spent on operator identity or dialect roles?
Is comprehend a consumer verb on a verb-neutral bias edge or a product? Is the outer disc the first ranked target, and how is the explosion (631 wonder anchors) budgeted?
Card format: should the parser keep a ~#k: datum's tag, set and path values, or should CLI cards switch to plain keys?

Which retention plane do overlays live on? Is #:overlay a new case and [reading] a new stance? Are reader roots declared in tracked workspace.spw or an untracked manifest, and do corpus walks skip them?
Does the arc cursor live in an overlay file or in LSP memory, and does a loop re-enter at beat 0 or at the phasor's phase?
Should the reading axis (author, prompt, research, creative) choose the default reducer and practice mode, or should personas be @(reader) scopes? Is grain the sanctioned complexity dial?
Where does a prediction live: ?{ } ~<prediction>, ?<next>, or % in the flow schedule? Is the schedule only a memory aid?
Is practice a per-reader setting, a per-surface default or both? What accuracy fades a mode? Should there be an opt-in, consumer-owned calibration ledger?
Retire the 48 templated read-aloud probes, or replace them with one instrumented probe per surface?

Should a dialect again be optional axes (surface lexer, lowering, vocabulary, voice) as in v0.1's phases? Can tagged block scalars embed another dialect under one active dialect per file? Should dialects be named as words with letters as aliases, and breaks: be lint-enforced?
How is 'spw' pronounced, and which word owns cut, expand, hub, lens, surface, measure, read and skim? Should domain practice, a celebration season, a hands_off relation and arc clocks be added?

Is care only a property of an inspection already done (a receipt), or also of a request (a declared aperture the tools honor)? If both, should resolveGranularity accept care, and how does care map to depth and plane without renaming either vocabulary?
Should #:review be derived from receipts rather than authored, with the gate enforcing the honesty rule?

Should glance-level disclosure (emit brief) carry claim status, given that it drops it today?
